card.law_is_about: Restructuring care-insurance financing, benefits and support for care recipients and their relatives.
card.they_want: Legally assured participation for care recipients and family caregivers in decisions at federal, state and local levels.
card.they_claim: According to Destatis, civil society performs around 86% of care work in Germany.
card.the_problem: The matching Destatis 86% statistic counts people cared for at home, including professional ambulatory care. It does not measure a work share. The exact source and intended shorthand remain unresolved.

claim_quote.original: Laut Statistischem Bundesamt werden rund 86 Prozent der Pflegearbeit in Deutschland von der Zivilgesellschaft erbracht
claim_quote.translation_en: Translation: According to the Federal Statistical Office, around 86 percent of care work in Germany is provided by civil society.

locator.paragraph: Second substantive paragraph, beginning Dabei gerät aus dem Fokus

counter_quote.original: Knapp neun von zehn Pflegebedürftigen (86 % beziehungsweise 4,9 Millionen) wurden im Dezember 2023 zu Hause versorgt.
counter_quote.translation_en: Translation: Almost nine in ten people needing care (86 percent or 4.9 million) were cared for at home in December 2023.

locator.section: Knapp neun von zehn Pflegebedürftigen wurden zu Hause versorgt

request_quote.translation_en: Translation: be involved on a binding basis.

correction: If using the identified Destatis release, describe 86% as the share of care recipients cared for at home, rather than the share of work performed by civil society. The release includes 1.1 million people partly or entirely served by professional ambulatory services. Do not substitute the 3.1 million predominantly family-care group as a corrected work-share denominator.
effect: The identified release cannot establish the precise national work-share assertion. It still documents a large home-care population, so it supports the broad importance of family-care participation.
limits: The author names Destatis but gives no specific release, year or table. A different statistic or loose language about home-care arrangements remains possible. No numerical share of unpaid work is established or disproven. Civil society is not operationally defined, and often does not say all care is unpaid. Family caregivers can also help people living in institutions. No intent or policy conclusion is inferred.
materiality_explanation: Potentially minor source/measure mismatch. The broad predominance of home care and request for participation survive; no quantified change to the actual work share has been established.
direction_explanation: Unknown: the actual work share is unestablished, so the numerical direction of a correction is unknown.
context_and_alternatives: Read and visually inspected both complete author pages, including the explicit binding-participation request and personal-care experience.
Destatis full release distinguishes home care from professional ambulatory provision and does not count hours or tasks.
Source-discovery searches did not establish a Destatis86% work-share statistic. Absence from search is not proof that no such statistic exists.
Primary WIdO 2020 report publicity uses a different home-care time-survey framework; no replacement national work ratio is inferred from it.

The June 5 text is context only, not independently authenticated as the exact version sent to this author. The source-measure question does not depend on a changed legal provision.
